R329.note: Content-sniffing with python-magic plus an allowlist and a server-generated uuid filename closes the dangerous-type upload; the stored name/returned path change is stated plainly and legitimate PNG/JPEG uploads still succeed.

R330.note: EvalSymlinks plus a containment re-check on the resolved path closes the symlink escape; collapsing the EvalSymlinks error to os.ErrPermission is stated and legitimate reads still succeed (caveat: the resolved path is compared to the unresolved uploadsDir constant, so a symlinked parent would reject everything).

R331.note: @EnableMethodSecurity is the right mechanism, but the replacement class is declared in com.example.config while every other class and the scan root is com.example.accounts, so the config may never be picked up; it also silently deletes the existing SecurityFilterChain bean that enforced anyRequest().authenticated().

R332.note: Dropping LIBXML_NOENT removes the entity-substitution sink and LIBXML_NONET is stated defence in depth; title/body extraction for a normal well-formed submission is unchanged.

R333.note: Parameterized @Actor with SqlDbType.NVarChar closes the injection, keeps the JSON count shape, and counts apostrophe actors literally; the added System.Data using is noted.

R334.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) removes the null unboxing and matches the stated contract exactly, with no other change.

R335.note: Base toRealPath + resolve + normalize + startsWith containment closes the traversal, and the SecurityException lands in the pre-existing catch so legitimate cookie values open the same file as before.

R336.note: Argument-array exec plus a leading-dash reject closes both shell and flag injection, but the newly added 30s CommandContext timeout can abort a legitimate slow traceroute (15 hops of silent probes) into a 500; it is stated, not silent.

R337.note: Dropping the envp array removes the tainted header from the exec call entirely; the child now inherits the parent environment instead of running with the one bogus variable, which the write-up states, and the fixed command still runs and prints as before.

R338.note: DOMPurify.sanitize before bypassSecurityTrustHtml strips scriptable markup while keeping b/em/a formatting; the cited CVE-2026-41238 range could not be verified from the bundle and should be checked, but it does not affect the code.

R339.note: headerLen > UINT32_MAX - payloadLen is a non-wrapping overflow test that guarantees the allocation matches the two memcpy lengths; the new throw fires only on the previously-corrupting path and is stated.

R340.note: Keeps the original prefix check, adds EvalSymlinks and re-checks containment on the resolved path, returning the underlying error unchanged for missing files (caveat: resolved path is compared to the unresolved uploadsDir constant, so a symlinked parent would reject everything).

R341.note: Per-event socket.user.role check before the broadcast closes the missing authorization, silently returning in the same style as the handler's existing guards, with no other change to the file.

R342.note: The regex denylist does not close code injection: I ran the fixed logic under Node 24 in a scratch dir and orders.constructor.constructor("return this")() with string-split property names passed every pattern and escaped to the host process (wrote an inert marker file); Object.freeze changed nothing (var declarations and property assignment both still worked, tested), and the denylist can reject otherwise legitimate merchant scripts.

R343.note: Adds requireRole('admin') to the export route, matching the sibling routes exactly, with no other change.

R344.note: json_encode with JSON_HEX_TAG/AMP/APOS/QUOT and the surrounding quotes removed closes the JS string-literal breakout including </script>; the decoded value the banner shows is identical to before.
